title: Example: architecture of a map editor

intents.title: The author creates and revises an architectural plan
intents.summary: An intention defines the desired result. Architectural components describe the system, and a route connects them through implementation steps. Edit this example or create your own map.
acceptanceCriteria: Text, components and links can be edited through forms.
A rejected candidate preserves the last accepted map.
After an explicit save, the map reopens with the same links.

intents.title: The developer receives a verifiable implementation plan
intents.summary: The second route shares the same validation and storage. Reuse references a common component by its ID.
acceptanceCriteria: Each step links to components and explanatory contracts.
Export preserves the identity of shared elements.

routes.title: From intention to a saved map

modules.title: Map model
modules.summary: Stores intentions, components, routes and stable references. Distinguishes a shared component from its occurrence in a route.

modules.title: Authoring interface
modules.summary: Provides forms for editing text and links. Shows architectural explanations above and all intention-led route lines below.

modules.title: Candidate validation
modules.summary: Checks references, intention lineage and consistent states before accepting changes.

modules.title: Storage adapter
modules.summary: Saves the accepted map through an explicit author action. The shared contract supports browser storage and temporary memory.

modules.title: Plan export
modules.summary: Builds readable Markdown from the accepted project while preserving architectural links.

chunks.name: An intention defines the result
chunks.body: Describe the property the system should provide and how the result will be checked. Criteria belong to the intention; a route offers a sequence for realising it.

chunks.name: Architectural element and route step
chunks.body: A component exists once in the map. A step references that component and an explanatory contract. Renaming preserves its ID and every link. Compare the two routes to see reuse.

chunks.name: Change acceptance contract
chunks.body: A form prepares a candidate. The shared engine validates the whole map. An error preserves the accepted project and the draft; successful validation permits an atomic replacement. Selecting a route step reveals this contract. Validate map performs the actual document check.

chunks.name: Storage contract
chunks.body: Applying changes and saving are separate actions. Save records the accepted map in this browser. If storage fails, JSON remains available for download. The second route uses the same adapter.

chunks.name: Plan handoff contract
chunks.body: Markdown presents intentions, architectural elements, contracts and routes. JSON preserves the structured source for further editing and import. Code references are supplied by the author; file existence is not checked automatically.

intersections.title: Shared validation across two routes
intersections.note: Both steps use one validator. The architecture defines the component once; the routes show its different occurrences.
